items.title: Fetch relay: routines read blocked hosts via a GitHub Actions fetch (docs/relay)
items.why: Four handoffs this week stalled only because the sandbox cannot reach ipo.gov.uk, nhs.uk, data.gov.uk, figma.com. A relay removes the whole class; the metrics routine gets Figma numbers too.
items.proof: handoffs citing 'no egress' drop to zero over the next 7 days; Figma metrics rows fill

items.title: Run watchdog: Telegram line when a scheduled routine leaves no commit/run-log line within 2h of its slot
items.why: The Wed 17:09 build was refused by the usage limit and nobody knew until the owner asked. Silence must be visible. Built 2026-09-25: scripts/run-watchdog.ts (+11 tests) appends one '| watchdog | missed:' RUNS line per silent slot; replayed against history it flags the 2026-09-23 17:00 build and nothing else. Only the workflow file is missing. Moved into .github/workflows by the interactive session 2026-09-28 (routine tokens lack the workflow scope).
items.proof: every missed slot produces one 'missed' bullet within 2h

items.title: Weekly ops retro routine (Sonnet): reads RUNS/ALERTS/git log, proposes prompt and tooling fixes as foundry queue items
items.why: Owner 2026-09-24: self-expansion is in scope; nobody currently reviews how the routines themselves perform. Built 2026-09-26: prompt (docs/routines/ops-retro.md) measuring slot reliability, throughput, blockers by cause, routine defects and owner load, writing docs/retros/<year>-W<week>.md and queuing proposals ≥ 4 here; watchdog slot Sat 07:59 in scripts/run-watchdog.ts; trigger created from the routine but create_trigger sets no repository, so the validation firing (session cse_01FzQ9gN1R2KVqFD6hTCvva6) stalled in 'requires action' with 0 tokens; trigger left disabled. Routine trig_015Uvn63XZUVqx1TAiWZrZL6 attached to the repo, set to Sonnet and enabled by the interactive session 2026-09-28; first run Saturday 2026-10-03 07:59 UTC.
items.proof: ≥ 2 accepted foundry items per month originate from the retro

items.title: Daily metrics routine fetches Figma/Chrome/AMO numbers through the relay instead of failing on egress
items.why: Every Figma row since launch says 'fetch failed: egress blocked'; no purchase/installs data at all. Done 2026-09-25: the metrics routine adopted the relay on its own (relay: metrics-2026-09-25, Figma versions API + plugin page fetched 200); the 2026-09-25 Variables Toolkit row reads 'via relay: install_count 0, like_count 0, view_count 2' — the proof number is in the row.
items.proof: Variables Toolkit metrics rows carry install/like numbers

items.title: Decide and implement what happens when Fable is exhausted mid-week (Opus fallback routine vs fewer runs)
items.why: Refused runs waste the slot; owner's allowance was gone by Wed 17:09 this week. Owner 2026-09-28: Opus may fill in only for low-complexity items. Built: routine trig_01GraXN5FPXmq5M9wJSYYeHN (Opus 5, 09:20 and 17:20 UTC) that stops if the Fable slot left a trace, else takes `npm run pipeline -- next --max-effort=0.3`.
items.proof: zero refused-run slots in a month

items.title: Let routines add or change GitHub Actions workflows (a CI job that syncs docs/ci/*.yml into .github/workflows/ using an owner PAT with the workflow scope)
items.why: 2026-09-25: the build routine finished the run watchdog but could not create its workflow file — git push and the GitHub API both refuse without the `workflow` scope. Every self-expansion item that needs a scheduled job hits this; today it cost the item. Owner added WORKFLOW_TOKEN 2026-09-28; installer workflow built and self-tested the same evening.
items.proof: a routine lands a new workflow without a handoff

items.title: Daily numbers row carries each refresh error's message, not just the source slug (metrics.mjs)
items.why: Repeat blocker: 2026-09-23 the nhs-ods error could not be fixed from a routine because refresh_log is unreachable from a sandbox and the row only named the slug (the interactive session had to read the D1 message); 2026-09-28 the row named uk-charities, uk-insolvency and uk-trademark-journal with no text again. metrics.mjs runs in CI with D1 access, so the fix is one query change: MAX(message) per slug, whitespace collapsed, pipes replaced, credential-shaped URL params redacted, 90 chars. From 2026-09-29 the build routine can fix a refresh error the morning it appears. Evidence 3 (two occurrences) × reach 2 (every gankdat source) ÷ 0.05 days.
items.proof: the next Daily numbers row with an error shows its message; a refresh error fixed by a routine within 24 h

items.title: Workflow installer: a CI job with WORKFLOW_TOKEN moves docs/ci/*.yml into .github/workflows (routines cannot)
items.why: Routine tokens lack the workflow scope (run-watchdog had to wait 3 days for the interactive session). With the owner's PAT as WORKFLOW_TOKEN a push touching docs/ci/ can install workflows automatically. Owner added WORKFLOW_TOKEN 2026-09-28; installer workflow built and self-tested the same evening.
items.proof: a workflow file added by a routine goes live without the interactive session

items.title: Queue items can carry a not_before date so dated checkpoints stop being offered early
items.why: The 09:00 build slot looked missed, and the fallback found only variables-toolkit/day-30-review, a checkpoint that cannot be done until 2026-10-21: every open queue was otherwise blocked. Without a date field a build run either fabricates the review or burns the slot, and the reviews keep adding day-7/day-30 checkpoints.
items.proof: npm run pipeline lists day-30-review under "scheduled" and does not offer it before 2026-10-21; it is offered again on the day

items.title: Self-caused notification list: triage and the weekly report recognise mail that our own automation triggered (Apify pricing, SAM key) and never escalate it
items.why: Three false alarms in one week, all caused by us. (1) scripts/publish-actors.mjs prices every actor PAY_PER_EVENT US$0.001/result (lines 62-71); Apify then mails the publisher 'Pricing change … $1.00/1,000 results' and triage filed two ALERTS handoffs (2026-09-27 18:07 uk-trademark-journal-watch, 2026-09-28 18:06 uk-gambling-commission) asking for a ledger check of a cost that does not exist — it is our own sale price; report 2026-W40 §6 then called it 'the highest-leverage open item'. (2) The SAM.gov key-rotation reminder became an owner: line on 2026-09-25 although sam-exclusions has read the keyless extract since 2026-09-20 (OUTSTANDING.md C1: owner acted, false alarm). Fix: docs/ops/SELF-CAUSED.md — a table pattern (sender, subject fragment) → cause (script/file) → what to log; the build routine adds a row in the same commit whenever it automates something that emails us (publishing, pricing, key rotation, DNS). Prompt sentence for the triage routine (Sonnet, hourly): 'Before classifying a store, vendor or platform mail, read docs/ops/SELF-CAUSED.md; a match is logged in docs/INBOX.md as `logged (self-caused: <cause>)` and never becomes an ALERTS.md line or a `needs owner`.' Same sentence for the weekly report before §3/§6. The prompt edits themselves are a handoff (RemoteTrigger API, interactive session). Evidence 3 (three occurrences) × reach 3 (triage 24×/day, report, owner) ÷ 0.2 days. Built 2026-09-29: docs/ops/SELF-CAUSED.md (8 self-caused rows, 3 agent-work rows, what is NOT self-caused), prompt mirrors docs/routines/inbox-triage.md and weekly-report.md with the sentence in place, CLAUDE.md rule. update_trigger refused both routines (created via http_api), so the live prompt edit is an ALERTS handoff.
items.proof: zero ALERTS/owner lines over 30 days that a later done:/OUTSTANDING line calls a false alarm; the two Apify pricing handoffs closed

items.title: Inbox triage searches unread mail without an age window, so a missed slot cannot lose mail
items.why: The hourly triage searches `newer_than:3h`; when slots are missed (GitHub cron gaps 2026-09-21/22, usage limits) the mail in between is never read. Nine unread threads dated 2026-09-18..21 surfaced only on 2026-09-28 17:07 by a manual catch-up (docs/INBOX.md 'Backlog catch-up'): the Gmail Send-as confirmation for info@gankdat.com (expired unclicked, owner had to redo it), Chrome Web Store identity verification (publishing unblocked a week late), the mcpservers.org approval, the Datarade application receipt. Fix: replace the search with `in:inbox is:unread` (no age filter) and mark each logged thread read in the same run (already done for triaged mail), so the window is the read state, not the clock; cap one run at 30 threads, oldest first, and note 'backlog' in the INBOX line when the mail is older than 3 h. Exact sentence for the triage prompt: 'Search Gmail for `in:inbox is:unread` (no newer_than filter): unread is the queue, so a missed slot only delays mail; process oldest first, at most 30 threads per run, mark each processed thread read, and write `(backlog)` after the timestamp of any thread older than 3 h.' Prompt edit is a handoff. Evidence 3 (9 threads, two owner-visible consequences) × reach 2 ÷ 0.1 days. Built 2026-09-30 (fallback): docs/routines/inbox-triage.md step 1 now reads the exact sentence above and step 2 carries the `(backlog)` marker; docs/SCHEDULERS.md names the new window. The live prompt replacement rides the existing 2026-09-29 ALERTS handoff (the routine was created via the HTTP API, so update_trigger refuses agents), which now covers both triage sentences in one edit.
items.proof: no 'backlog' or 'found unread' INBOX line over 30 days; every store mail logged within 2 h of arrival

items.title: Daily numbers row measures change-feed use (MCP get_changes + REST /v1/changes over 7 days), which STRATEGY §4 targets but nothing counts
items.why: STRATEGY §4 target 'Change-feed calls / week: 50' and the proofs of change-feed-upsell (done 2026-09-24, ≥ 50 calls/week) and trademark-watch-surface (done 2026-09-28) cannot be read anywhere: ventures/gankdat/scripts/metrics.mjs has no change-feed query, and the REST routes write no traffic data point at all — only /mcp (routes/mcp.ts) and /x402 (x402/routes.ts) call TRAFFIC.writeDataPoint — so review 2026-W39 §1 records 'unknown, likely 0'. Fix: (a) the /v1/changes and /v1/data handlers write a fire-and-forget data point (blob1 rest_changes|rest_data, blob2 UA, blob3 path, blob5 source slug; no IP, same shape as mcp_authed); (b) metrics.mjs adds one Analytics Engine query — blob5 LIKE '%get_changes%' on mcp_authed plus blob1 = 'rest_changes', 7 days — and prints `changes 7d: N (mcp M, rest R)`; (c) STRATEGY §4 row names that column as its source. Evidence 3 (a target and two proofs unmeasurable) × reach 3 (review, report, build decide on it) ÷ 0.15 days.
items.proof: the Daily numbers row carries `changes 7d:` from the first run; review 2026-W40 fills the change-feed row with a number

items.title: Daily numbers row carries Apify actor runs and users from the Apify API (APIFY_TOKEN already in CI)
items.why: STRATEGY §4 target 'Apify paid runs / month: 100' is unmeasured — review 2026-W39 §4: 'no run count reaches the repo'. All 17 actors went public on 2026-09-28 (RUNS 21:30), so from now the shelf either produces runs or it does not, and no routine can see which. The token exists: gankdat-publish.yml passes secrets.APIFY_TOKEN to scripts/publish-actors.mjs. Fix: docs/ci/gankdat-metrics.yml (the workflow installer moves it) adds APIFY_TOKEN to the metrics step; metrics.mjs calls GET https://api.apify.com/v2/acts?my=1&limit=100 and sums the per-actor stats (totalRuns, totalUsers30Days — confirm field names from the first response in the CI log), printing `apify: R runs (+d/24h), U users/30d, P public`; the +d comes from yesterday's row. Evidence 3 × reach 3 (the §4 target, review, report) ÷ 0.15 days.
items.proof: the row carries `apify:` from the first run; the first paid run is visible in the row within 24 h of happening

items.title: A store approval or rejection mail updates the venture's STORE.md status line in the triage commit, so the metrics routine reads the live listing the next morning
items.why: Store state reaches ALERTS.md but not the files the routines read. Firefox AMO tentatively approved ReadFocus and Highlight Keep on 2026-09-22 22:25/22:40 (INBOX), yet both STORE.md files still say 'awaiting review' and venture.json 'building' on 2026-09-29 — seven days, flagged by review 2026-W39 §2 and again by report 2026-W40 §2, and the daily metrics routine has read 'not live yet' for both every day since. mcpservers.org approval (2026-09-21) reached the listings log only on 2026-09-28. Fix: exact sentence for the triage prompt: 'A mail from a store or directory that approves, publishes, rejects or takes down one of our listings also updates that venture's STORE.md status line (and venture.json status when a first listing goes live) in the same commit, citing the mail's date; then the ALERTS line is informational.' Plus one build-routine step now: record the two AMO listings as tentatively approved 2026-09-22 with their URLs so the metrics routine starts reading them. Prompt edit is a handoff. Evidence 2 (three listings, two reviews flagged it) × reach 2 (metrics daily, review, report) ÷ 0.1 days.
items.proof: AMO Daily check rows show install counts instead of 'not live yet'; no review/report flags an unrecorded listing over 30 days

items.title: Fallback routine detects a late Fable slot, not just a missed one, before it starts building
items.why: Today the 09:00 Fable build committed at 09:28, 8 minutes after the 09:20 fallback had run its STEP 0 check and concluded the slot was missed. Both built, and the push collided: a merge conflict in queues/foundry.json that had to be resolved by hand (this run kept both sides; a less careful resolution loses one routine's work). The check can only see a slot that has already committed, so any Fable run slower than 20 minutes triggers the same race, twice a day. Options for the fix: have the build routine write a `| build | started` run-log line (or a docs/ops/RUNNING lock file) at the top of its run so the fallback can see an in-flight slot; or move the fallback to +45 min; or have the fallback re-check immediately before its commit and rebase rather than merge. Cheapest is the started-line: one sentence in the build prompt, one check in the fallback prompt. SECOND OCCURRENCE the same day (evidence, not a new item): the 17:00 Fable build committed at 17:29:57, 9 minutes after the 17:20 fallback's STEP 0 check, and both built the SAME item (self-caused-alerts) — the fallback's duplicate was discarded on merge, so a whole Opus slot produced only the closure work Fable had left undone. Twice in one day now; the check cannot see a slot that has not committed yet. THIRD OCCURRENCE 2026-09-30 (evidence, not a new item): the 09:00 Fable build committed at 09:27:37, six minutes after the 09:21 STEP 0 check, so every collision so far has been inside a 6-9 minute window after the check. This one cost no duplicated work — Fable took gankdat `claude-directory-listing` and the fallback a foundry item — but still produced the same three-file merge conflict (ALERTS, RUNS, STRATEGY, all end-of-file appends) resolved by hand. Three collisions in two days across both slots; a started-line or lock the fallback can read before STEP 0 is the only option that closes the window, since moving the fallback later only moves it.
items.proof: no second collision over 30 days: no merge conflict between a build and a fallback commit, and no day with both a `(build)` and a `(fallback)` commit inside 30 minutes
